en.name: Eugene IV
en.summary: A pope whose stormy conflict with the Council of Basel forced him briefly from Rome, while his own rival Council of Florence achieved a short-lived reunion with the Greek church.
en.body: Eugene IV's reign was dominated by a protracted power struggle with the Council of Basel, which asserted conciliar authority over the pope and at one point declared him deposed in favor of an antipope; Eugene responded by relocating his own rival council, eventually to Florence, where in 1439 it achieved a dramatic, if ultimately short-lived, formal reunion with the Greek Orthodox Church, undone soon after by the fall of Constantinople. He was twice driven from Rome by local revolt during his turbulent papacy.
